best_parts: node c3: brown-in-gallbladder and black-in-gallbladder are each one association swap (site or colour), so a miss diagnoses which pairing the learner has wrong
nodes c5 and c6: TR23 tested twice in different forms (contrast, then ICU vignette), and c5's 'milder since no stone' and 'lower mortality since younger' are two distinct wrong models
node c8: the PYQ-key probe with feedback c8_t1 naming the wrong model (classic picture of pure cholesterol) and c8_t2 conceding the textbook line is real
flaws: node c4q: 'chronic haemolysis' and 'cirrhosis' are tagged TR15 but are not association swaps for cholesterol risk factors; the only hormone-linked option is the key, so the item is findable by content, and the trap label does not match what the distractors test
node c6: 'low risk since no stone' and 'mild, safe to observe' both express the same wrong model (no stone means benign), so they do not separate two errors

node start_t1 and start_t2 (and the other feedback nodes): every wrong option offers only retry; after a second miss there is no different second explanation and no show-the-answer route, so the remediation is the same technique

best_parts: node show_start: a step-by-step worked explanation reached by agency on a first miss, a genuinely different second explanation from the probe that failed
node c2: 'black from bile infection' and 'brown from chronic haemolysis' are each one colour or cause swap, and the feedback c2_t15b refutes via the cause-to-stone pairing
node c4 with c4_t23a and c4_t23b: two milder-course distractors, each refuted by the mechanism (stasis and ischaemia) with a claim
flaws: node start_t1: 'pure cholesterol, the commonest in texts' is tagged TR1 on a haemolysis stem that never asks for the commonest type; no one who knows the haemolysis pairing would pick it, so it is dominated for O3 and a miss cannot be diagnosed
node c3: a two-option binary probe (pure cholesterol versus mixed) with one trap and only a hint as the alternative; it is the only O2 test on the main path, so the exam-key objective is thin
node c4: the single O8 probe; the key 'Worse, with more gangrene and perforation' is the only option not framed as 'milder', so it is findable by form, and TR23 is not re-tested in this segment

best_parts: node acal_v: the ICU burns vignette with TR23 'mild, watch' and TR4 'settles with analgesia, as in biliary colic' as wrong options, a cross-trap that retests colic against cholecystitis in a new setting
node pyq and pyq_t_chol: the exam-entry drill, where the textbook-commonest wrong model is named and refuted with the exam-key convention, and 'Show me why' gives a second route
node acal_p: 'milder since no stone' and 'lower mortality since younger' separate two wrong models, each with feedback that names the model and gives the repair
flaws: the correct option is the first listed on every probe (pyq, black_p, brown_p, acal_p, acal_v), so the key is findable by position; this breaks DP1 and drives the R2 score down

node pyq_t_black: 'black pigment stones' on a 'most common type' question is a filler tagged TR15 (the trap map marks pigment options as partial for TR1), and it is dominated: a tired student would pick cholesterol or mixed over it
node brown_p: both wrong options pair black stones with haemolysis, one site-swapped and one colour-swapped, so they test one wrong model twice rather than two
